subject: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway and mutual action plan
messages:
From: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@luminr.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@luminr.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway + next steps

Hi Priya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo this morning. Quick recap of what we walked through and the proposed acceptance pathway so we can align on next steps: 

- Demo coverage: streaming chat with progressive decode, batch inference for async scoring, and short-form completion paths.
- Candidate acceptance criteria (provisional):
  • API latency (interactive chat): p95 <= 300 ms; p99 <= 600 ms
  • Streaming chunk latency (first-byte p95): <= 200 ms for 90% of messages
  • Sustained throughput: ~120–150 requests/sec during peak 10-min windows
  • Concurrency target: support bursts up to 200 concurrent open sessions with KV cache warming
  • Error budget: <0.2% 5xx on production traffic

Attached: luminr-slo-checklist.xlsx (worksheet with acceptance gates), demo-traffic-sample.jsonl (representative traffic we used).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the acceptance gates above (or note adjustments) — Priya (by EOD Thu)
2) We run a two-week pilot with synthetic replay of your demo traffic (owner: Redwood SE)
3) Procurement: provide SOC2 + contract template; we’ll hand over a procurement pack (owner: Luminr Procurement)
4) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) doc — draft attached, we’ll iterate and lock dates

Please call out any deal blockers up front (e.g., strict on-promise p95 SLA, required region, or data residency). I’ll loop in Hannah from CS to coordinate pilot checkpoints if you confirm the acceptance gates.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: luminr-slo-checklist.xlsx, demo-traffic-sample.jsonl

From: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@luminr.ai>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@luminr.ai>
Cc: Luminr Procurement <procurement@luminr.ai>
Date: 2028-08-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway + next steps

Aisha —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we sign-off on the MAP: 

1) Latency tolerance: our primary UX goal is sub-300ms perceived latency on short prompts (under 80 tokens). For streamed responses we care more about time-to-first-chunk — 85% of interactions should see a first chunk within 180ms.

2) Concurrency/throughput: the 120–150 rps range is accurate for our pilot, but production expectations are higher — we expect to scale to sustained 400 rps over a quarter (multi-tenant inference across product features). For acceptance we’ll validate headroom: pilot should demonstrate linear scaling to 2x the pilot peak.

3) Long tail behavior: we need p99 guidance under typical load; if p99 spikes above 1s we’ll need fallback rules.

4) Data residency: pilot in us-central is fine; production may need EU region for a subset of traffic. Please flag any cross-region limitations.

I’ve attached the brief procurement checklist for legal (will send contract redlines separately).

—Priya
CTO, Luminr Health
attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@luminr.ai>, aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway + next steps

Thanks Priya — great notes. Short replies and a proposed MAP revision: 

- Latency: we can target interactive p95 <= 275 ms on the pilot cluster by tuning batching and KV cache TTLs; p99 will be monitored and we’ll set automated circuit-breakers at 1s.
- Concurrency/Throughput: for the pilot we’ll size for 2x pilot peak headroom (i.e., if pilot traffic peaks at 150 rps we’ll provision for 300 rps and validate autoscaling to 600 rps as the stress test). For production EU routing we recommend dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Streaming: we’ll instrument first-byte timers and provide dashboards; default chunk size will be 256 tokens but we can tune to 128 if you see chunking latency hitting thresholds.

Action items (proposed owners & dates):
- Redwood to deliver MAP v2 (with explicit test dates & pass/fail gates) — Ben (2028-08-06)
- SE baseline run + replay results (with traffic envelope & short report) — Rachel (start 2028-08-08, result by 2028-08-10)
- Procurement packet + SOC2 evidence — Luminr procurement (please confirm ETA)
- Pilot kickoff & weekly checkpoints — Hannah (coordinate cadence once pilot window confirmed)

I’ve attached a draft MAP (mutual-action-plan.docx) and will incorporate Priya’s comments.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx

From: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@luminr.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-05T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway + next steps

Priya / team —

Quick technical notes from the SE perspective based on the demo traces: 

- Replay approach: we’ll run three replay modes — (1) pilot-realistic (1:1 timing), (2) burst stress (3x instantaneous rps), and (3) mixed multi-session to validate KV cache warming.
- Observability: we’ll push dashboards with token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 for both non-stream and stream-first-chunk metrics, and a trace link per failed request.
- Pilot config (proposal): 3x optimized inference nodes, continuous batching window 5–10ms, KV cache TTL 60s for warming. If you want faster first-chunk, reduce continuous batching and use a smaller chunk size — there's a throughput/latency tradeoff we can tune during the pilot.
- Fallbacks: we recommend two fallback policies during pilot: (A) degrade model to faster quantized variant at load thresholds, (B) limit streaming chunk size with an explicit notice to UX for long-form responses.

I’ll start the baseline replay on 2028-08-08 once we confirm traffic sample. Expect an initial report by 2028-08-10.

—Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: demo-traffic-sample.jsonl

From: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@luminr.ai>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-07T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance acceptance pathway + next steps

Thanks all — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. Confirming:

- We accept the provisional acceptance gates (Priya) with the caveat that production will require EU-region separation for a subset of EU patient data.
- Procurement: procurement will send the contract redlines by 2028-08-09.
- Pilot: Luminr confirms pilot start window 2028-08-08 to 2028-08-21; we expect the baseline replay results by 2028-08-10 and a short readout on 2028-08-11.

One ask: Ben / Rachel — please include a short appendix in the MAP that lists the measurable pass/fail criteria per gate (explicit numbers for p95/p99/first-chunk and the traffic envelope used). That will help Legal/Procurement sign off quicker.

Looking forward to the pilot.

—Priya
CTO, Luminr Health
